stories.head: US, Russia and Ukraine open two days of talks in Abu Dhabi
stories.say: American, Russian and Ukrainian delegations began two days of talks in Abu Dhabi on Tuesday, the first such meeting since February. Volodymyr Zelenskyy called day one constructive.
stories.stand: The first three-way meeting since February focused on security guarantees, with both sides still far apart on territory.
body: Delegations from the US, Russia and Ukraine began a two-day session in Abu Dhabi on Tuesday aimed at ending the war. It is the first three-way meeting since February, according to CBS News and AP.

Ukraine's team is led by Rustem Umerov and Russia's by Kremlin aide Vladimir Medinsky. Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner represent the US. Volodymyr Zelenskyy called the first day constructive and said humanitarian issues and security guarantees were discussed.

Russia wants Ukraine to withdraw from four regions Moscow annexed in 2022 and to give up on NATO membership. Kyiv rejects giving up territory and wants an immediate ceasefire. Al Jazeera reported that European governments met the Ukrainian delegation separately.

stories.head: Qatar says it sees progress in US-Iran talks
stories.say: Qatar said on Tuesday it sees progress in talks between Washington and Tehran, a day after its prime minister met Donald Trump at the White House.
stories.stand: Doha, a key mediator, would not say how close a deal is, as Trump held off fresh strikes but kept the naval blockade.
body: Qatar said on Tuesday it saw progress in talks between the US and Iran, a day after Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani met Donald Trump at the White House.
A Qatari foreign ministry spokesman, Ibrahim bin Sultan Al Hashmi, said Doha could not say how close or far away an agreement was. He called for the Strait of Hormuz to reopen as soon as possible.

Euronews reported that Trump said Gulf states had urged him to hold off on new strikes and that he would do so for now, while keeping the US naval blockade. Tehran has proposed resuming talks within two days if the US halts attacks and lifts its blockade of Iranian ports.

stories.head: Israel's new Knesset sworn in amid heckling and walkouts
stories.say: Israel's new parliament was sworn in on Tuesday, three weeks after a deadlocked election. Arab lawmakers walked out during Benjamin Netanyahu's speech.
stories.stand: Caretaker prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu attacked Arab-Israeli lawmakers, while rival Gadi Eisenkot has the first chance to form a government.
body: Israel's new Knesset was sworn in on Tuesday, three weeks after a deadlocked election, ABC News reported. The ceremony was marked by heckling inside and a protest outside.
Benjamin Netanyahu, still caretaker prime minister, used his speech to accuse Arab-Israeli lawmakers of backing Hamas. Members of the United Arab List walked out, as did Democrats leader Yair Golan.

Netanyahu's Likud holds 29 of the 120 seats. Former military chief Gadi Eisenkot has been given the first chance to form a government. Euronews also reported that Eisenkot had been tasked with forming a coalition.

stories.head: Saudi Arabia says it shot down missiles fired at Riyadh
stories.say: The Saudi-led coalition says it destroyed a ballistic missile and a cruise missile over Riyadh on Tuesday, a day after an attack on a major oil pipeline.
stories.stand: The coalition blamed Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis, who had no immediate comment, after a Monday attack on the East-West pipeline.
body: The Saudi-led coalition fighting Yemen's Houthis said it intercepted a ballistic missile and a cruise missile over Riyadh on Tuesday, and another ballistic missile over the south.

Coalition spokesman Major-General Turki al-Maliki blamed the Iran-backed Houthis, who had no immediate comment. Residents received shelter alerts before civil defence said the danger had passed, Al Jazeera reported, citing AFP.
On Monday the East-West pipeline in the Medina region was attacked. A Saudi energy ministry official said it caused a limited fire that was put out, with no injuries.

stories.head: Gulf states agree joint military command post in Kuwait
stories.say: The six Gulf Cooperation Council states agreed on Tuesday to set up a military command post in Kuwait and station forces there, after a meeting of defence ministers in Bahrain.
stories.stand: No opening date, troop numbers or duties were announced for the post, which will sit within the bloc's Unified Military Command.
body: The six members of the Gulf Cooperation Council agreed on Tuesday to set up a military command post in Kuwait and to station forces there, the bloc's secretary-general, Jasem Mohamed Albudaiwi, said.
The decision followed a meeting of defence ministers from Bahrain, Kuwait, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia and the UAE in Manama, Euronews reported. No opening date, troop numbers or duties were given.
The post will be part of the Unified Military Command set up in 2013, whose main headquarters opened in Riyadh in 2021. Al Jazeera also reported the decision.

stories.head: Twelve killed in fog-bound motorway pile-up in Bulgaria
stories.say: Twelve people were killed and fifty injured in a pile-up of about fifty vehicles in thick fog on Bulgaria's A1 motorway near Yambol. Wednesday is a day of mourning.
stories.stand: Officials said the crash began with a collision between a bus and a lorry about 75 km west of Burgas.
body: Twelve people died and 50 were injured in a motorway pile-up in thick fog near Yambol in eastern Bulgaria, ABC News reported. Officials said fog was the likely cause.
An interior ministry official, Lyubomir Nikolov, said it began with a collision between a bus and a lorry about 75 km west of Burgas. The regional governor said about 50 vehicles were involved.
Health minister Katya Ivkova said 11 people died at the scene and one in hospital. Prime Minister Rumen Radev declared Wednesday a day of mourning. Euronews published aerial footage of the scene.

stories.head: Mexico arrests cartel cell leader wanted by the US
stories.say: Mexican authorities have arrested Rafael Alvarez, known as R2, a leader of a Jalisco cartel cell wanted in the US. He was wounded in a shootout near Guadalajara.
stories.stand: Mexico's security secretary said the arrest in Zapopan relied on information shared by the US Drug Enforcement Administration.
body: Mexican authorities announced on Sunday the arrest of Rafael Alvarez, known as R2, a leader of a Jalisco New Generation Cartel cell, in Zapopan, Jalisco. Another 19 people were arrested with him.

Security Secretary Omar Garcia Harfuch said Alvarez was wounded in a shootout and is receiving medical care. He said the operation used information shared by the US Drug Enforcement Administration, which says Alvarez is wanted on drug trafficking and firearms charges.
Authorities allege he is linked to killings, extortion of avocado businesses and the 2025 killing of a mayor. CBS News reported the details, citing AFP.

stories.head: Dozens of migrants die off Crete and Senegal
stories.say: Greece's coast guard recovered thirteen bodies from a boat south of Crete on Monday, and one rescued person later died. Off Senegal, a boat capsized, leaving at least thirty-nine dead.
stories.stand: More than 180 people were found on boats south of Crete, while only one passenger survived a capsizing off Kébémer.
body: Greece's coast guard recovered 13 bodies from a boat south of Crete early on Monday, CBS News reported, citing AP. One of the 18 people rescued from it later died, bringing the toll to 14.
The coast guard said more than 180 people were found on three boats on Monday morning. Two Sudanese nationals were arrested as suspected smugglers.

Off Senegal, a boat bound for Spain capsized near Kébémer on Sunday. Emergency services said on Monday the toll had risen to 39, with one passenger rescued alive. Euronews also reported the Senegal deaths.

stories.head: Cameroon sets February date for twice-delayed elections
stories.say: Cameroon's president, Paul Biya, has set the seventh of February next year for legislative and local elections that have already been postponed twice.
stories.stand: The 93-year-old, who has ruled since 1982, announced the date in a decree read on public radio.
body: Cameroon's legislative and local elections will be held on 7 February 2027, President Paul Biya announced in a decree read on public radio on Monday, Al Jazeera reported. The polls have been postponed twice.
Biya, 93, has ruled since 1982 and is the world's oldest head of state. His re-election in October 2025 sparked protests.
Lawmakers' terms have been extended to 20 December and municipal councillors' terms to 28 February 2027.

stories.say: Japan has agreed to give the Philippine military a coastal radar system and surveillance drones, a grant worth four point three billion yen, to help track ships.
stories.stand: The equipment is meant to help protect shipping routes including the South China Sea, a programme Beijing has criticised.
body: Japan agreed to give the Philippine military a coastal radar system and surveillance drones under a grant worth 4.3 billion yen, Euronews reported. The deal was signed in Manila.
Philippine Foreign Secretary Maria Theresa Lazaro and Japan's ambassador, Katsuro Kitagawa, signed it. The radar goes to the navy and the drones to the air force.
Japan's foreign ministry says the equipment will help protect shipping routes, including in the South China Sea. Beijing has criticised the programme.

stories.head: Pope Leo draws an estimated 650,000 to Mass in Córdoba
stories.say: Pope Leo the Fourteenth celebrated Mass in Córdoba, Argentina, on Tuesday before a crowd officials put at six hundred and fifty thousand, a day after huge crowds in Buenos Aires.
stories.stand: The pope urged Argentines to follow the example of their saints before a final Mass in Luján and a trip to Peru.
body: Pope Leo XIV celebrated Mass in Córdoba, Argentina, on Tuesday before a crowd officials estimated at 650,000, Euronews reported. The city had gone nearly 40 years without a papal visit.
He urged Argentines to follow the example of their saints, including José Gabriel del Rosario Brochero. The day before, an estimated 2.5 million people turned out to see him in Buenos Aires.
A final Mass is planned in Luján on Wednesday before he travels to Peru. Al Jazeera reported that he met survivors of clergy abuse during the visit.

stories.say: Okinawa's governor, Genta Koja, says he will ask for a review of the agreement covering American troops in Japan, after a US marine was charged over a woman's death.
stories.stand: The move follows the indictment of a US marine accused of killing a woman at a hotel in Naha in October; he denies it.
body: Okinawa Governor Genta Koja said on Monday he would request a review of the 1960 Japan-US Status of Forces Agreement, CBS News reported, citing AFP. Critics say it gives the US military preferential treatment.

It follows the death of a 39-year-old woman at a hotel in Naha on 3 October. Prosecutors have indicted a US marine, Lance Corporal Devin Jacob Ballard, 20, on suspicion of her killing. He denies the allegations.
About 54,000 US military personnel are based in Japan, and Okinawa hosts about 70% of US military facilities there.

stories.say: Russia's list of unfriendly countries, set up in 2022, now shapes court rulings, property and debts. Import duties on spirits from those countries rose from twenty to thirty-five per cent.
stories.stand: A Putin decree lets Russian debtors withhold payments to creditors in listed countries, which include the US, UK and EU members.
body: Russia's list of unfriendly countries, set by government order in March 2022, now affects courts, property and debts, Euronews reported. It includes the US, the UK, Canada, Japan, Ukraine and EU members.

Russia's Supreme Court cited the list when declining to return a child to France. A bill in the Duma would allow vehicles stolen from listed countries to be registered.

stories.stand: The author had tried and failed to get a High Court injunction to stop the investigation being published.
body: A joint investigation by ITV News and The Guardian, published on Tuesday, reports that several women accuse the children's author David Walliams of pursuing them sexually when they were teenagers. The allegations date back to 2003.

stories.stand: Fixed-term prisoners now serve a third of their sentence rather than half, unless their offence is exempt.
body: About 650 prisoners were freed on Tuesday in the third wave of the expanded early release scheme in England and Wales, ITV News reported.

Ministry of Justice figures put the prison population at 86,982 on Monday, up from 86,883 a week earlier.

stories.head: US moves refuelling planes from RAF Mildenhall over threat
stories.say: The US military moved refuelling planes from RAF Mildenhall in Suffolk to bases in Germany, Spain and Scotland on Monday. A US official called it a proactive step over a threat.
stories.stand: The Wall Street Journal reported the threat was linked to Iran; Downing Street said British air bases are safe.
body: The US military moved KC-135 refuelling planes from RAF Mildenhall in eastern England on Monday, CBS News and ITV News reported. Aircraft went to bases in Germany, Spain and Scotland.

A US official told AP the move was proactive rather than reactive and that some aircraft may return. A US Air Force spokesperson said aircraft rotate between bases routinely. The Wall Street Journal first reported, citing unnamed sources, that the threat was linked to Iran.
The prime minister's office said British air bases are safe. Less than two months ago, the US withdrew bombers from RAF Fairford after a suspected Iran-linked plot.

stories.stand: Prosecutors say the alleged network included Iran's Revolutionary Guards and Kata'ib Hizballah; Iran denies involvement.
body: US prosecutors in Manhattan unsealed a superseding indictment charging three men over nearly 20 planned attacks on Jewish communities in Europe and the US, ABC News reported, citing AP.

stories.say: Russell Brand has been jailed for ten and a half years at Southwark Crown Court for raping one woman and sexually assaulting three others. He will be on the sex offenders' register for life.
stories.stand: The comedian was convicted of one count of rape and three of sexual assault, and cleared of three other counts.
body: Russell Brand, 51, was sentenced to 10 and a half years at Southwark Crown Court on Monday for one count of rape and three of sexual assault, ITV News and CBS News reported.

Mr Justice Bennathan gave him nine years for the rape and 18 months for the sexual assaults. He was acquitted of two other rape counts and one count of attempted indecent assault. He will be on the sex offenders' register for life.

body: Prime Minister Andy Burnham declined to give the Independent Office for Police Conduct his full confidence, ITV News reported on Monday. It followed criticism by the family of an 18-year-old murdered in Hampshire.

stories.head: Civil servant convicted of fraud for holding five jobs at once
stories.say: A civil servant from east London has been convicted of fraud for holding up to five full-time government jobs at once. He earned almost three hundred and fifty thousand pounds.
stories.stand: Kashim Chowdhury used remote working and sick notes; at one point he was contracted for 183 hours a week.
body: A civil servant, Kashim Chowdhury, 56, from Whitechapel, east London, was convicted at Southwark Crown Court on Monday of nine counts of fraud, ITV News reported.

At one point he was contracted to work 183 hours a week. The Crown Prosecution Service will seek to recover the money in a proceeds of crime hearing.

stories.stand: The public has 60 days to comment; labour advocates say the rule would be hard for jobless workers to meet.
body: The US Department of Labor proposed stricter federal rules on Monday for people claiming unemployment benefits, CBS News reported. Claimants would need to make at least five unique work searches a week.
Many states currently require two or three, four require five and some require only one. States could count other activities and use a points system.
The proposal was due in the Federal Register on Tuesday, opening a 60-day comment period. Labour advocates say it would be hard to meet and costly for states to run.

body: China's trade surplus for January to October reached $1.04 trillion, according to General Administration of Customs data released on Tuesday, Euronews reported. Last year the milestone came in November.

stories.head: Alzheimer's mutations disrupt nerve-muscle links in lab model
stories.say: Florida researchers found mutations linked to inherited Alzheimer's disrupted signals between nerve and muscle cells, in a lab model with no brain at all.
stories.stand: The University of Central Florida study used a human-cell system without a brain or spinal cord.
body: Mutations linked to rare inherited Alzheimer's disrupted communication between motor neurons and muscle cells in a human-cell model with no brain or spinal cord, ScienceDaily reported.
The researchers say this suggests some early movement problems may begin outside the brain. The study was led by James Hickman of the University of Central Florida, with the company Hesperos.

The lead researcher, Wei-Na Zhang of a state laboratory in Beijing, described the human results as proof of concept for feasibility rather than direct validation.

stories.head: Fossil fuel emissions set to dip in 2026, but total CO2 still rises
stories.say: Fossil fuel emissions are projected to fall zero point four per cent this year, but total carbon dioxide emissions, including land use, will still rise, the Global Carbon Budget says.
stories.stand: Scientists say the drop is driven partly by the Iran war energy shock and is not a lasting peak.
body: Fossil carbon dioxide emissions are projected to fall 0.4% in 2026, according to the Global Carbon Budget published on Tuesday, Euronews reported. Oil emissions are expected to fall 1.9%, while coal rises 0.6%.
Total emissions including land use are projected at 43.3 billion tonnes, up from 42.8 billion in 2025, partly because of peat fires in Southeast Asia.

The remaining carbon budget is put at 150 billion tonnes, under four years at current rates. Study lead Pierre Friedlingstein of the University of Exeter said a drop driven by geopolitical shocks is not a sustainable solution.

stories.head: COP31 opens in Antalya with electrification at the top of the agenda
stories.say: The COP31 climate talks opened in Antalya, Turkey, on Monday. The hosts want electricity to meet thirty-five per cent of world energy demand by twenty thirty-five.
stories.stand: The US has no official delegation, and the transition away from fossil fuels is not on the formal agenda.
body: The UN climate summit COP31 opened in Antalya, Turkey, on Monday and runs until 20 November, Euronews and Al Jazeera reported. Turkey holds the presidency while Australia steers the negotiations.

Turkey is launching a non-binding pledge for electricity to meet at least 35% of global energy demand by 2035, up from about a fifth now. Climate advocates say it does not require the extra power to be low-carbon.
The US has no official delegation. The transition away from fossil fuels is not on the formal agenda. COP31 president Murat Kurum said the hosts would not lower their ambition.

stories.head: Flash heating could turn old wind turbine blades into useful materials
stories.say: Researchers at Tsinghua University heated old wind turbine blades to about two thousand degrees in seconds, turning them into silicon carbide and graphene.
stories.stand: Europe's waste from decommissioned blades is projected to rise from 20,000 tonnes in 2025 to 55,000 tonnes by 2030.
body: Researchers at Tsinghua University in China used flash joule heating to heat wind turbine blades to about 2,000°C in seconds, Euronews reported. The process turns them into silicon carbide and graphene.

Blades are hard to recycle. Europe's decommissioned blade waste is projected to rise from 20,000 tonnes in 2025 to 55,000 tonnes by 2030.
